about.title: Tehama Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Tehama sits along a stretch of rural highway network where State Route 36, State Route 32, South Avenue, and the corridor near 6700 Sr-36(w) carry a steady mix of local and through traffic. Public records show 4 injury collisions and 4 people hurt in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Friday nights between midnight and 2 a.m. Whether your collision happened on a state highway or a quieter county road, sorting out fault, insurance calls, and medical bills afterward is a lot to manage on your own. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, that can put you in touch with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Tehama County claims. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Getting guidance early, before evidence disappears or you speak with an insurer, can make a real difference in how your claim unfolds.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Soon After a Tehama Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity, like a county road authority, might be responsible. An attorney can help sort out which deadline applies to your situation early on.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage of blame assigned to you can reduce your compensation, even if you were mostly not at fault. Insurance adjusters know this and may try to shift blame during a recorded statement, so it's wise to get guidance before speaking with them.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get informed about your rights after a Tehama crash. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, which is one more reason to understand your claim's full value before settling.

items.question: I was in a crash on SR-36 near Tehama and the insurance company already called me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce your claim's value later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Tehama County?
items.answer: California's standard statute of limitations for personal injury is two years from the date of the crash. If your accident may involve a government entity, such as a poorly maintained county road, that deadline could be as short as six months, so it helps to get advice sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your award may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it important to have someone evaluate the details of your crash rather than accepting an insurer's initial assessment.
